title: Advertisement in Media to Raise Awareness for Government Policies and Programmes
what_it_is: Advertisement in Media to Raise Awareness for Government Policies and Programmes

sections.label: Government advertising platform choices
sections.summary: MCI decides advertising platforms based on content, target demographic, media habits and language, citing Merdeka Generation and COVID-19 examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information what are the considerations used to decide whether and, in what way, to deploy print, TV or radio advertising to raise awareness of specific Government policies or programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: These include television, radio, print, digital display panels, online platforms, such as websites, social media, WhatsApp, as well as ground outreach activities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The choice of platforms is determined by a variety of factors, including the nature of the content, our target demographic segment, their media consumption habits and language preferences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: For example, to raise awareness of the Merdeka Generation Package, the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) focused on traditional media, including television (TV) and radio and print, and engaged seniors face-to-face through Merdeka Generation roadshows, community events and home visits, given the profile of the target audience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: For the Coronavirus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19) communication, MCI has used print, radio, TV, digital display panels at Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates, Gov.sg social media sites and the dialect belt on Channel 8 to reach the widest possible audience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: MCI also uses Gov.sg WhatsApp to push out daily notifications in all four languages to 653,000 subscribers on case updates, as well as health advisories and corrections of misinformation.

sections.label: Awareness and citizen action
sections.summary: Responsible citizen action requires awareness of issues and facts, and whether awareness or action is needed depends on need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In order for one to take action as a responsible citizen, one needs to be aware of what the issues are and understand what the facts are.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, the answer to Mr Perera's question is, it is both, depending on need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Sometimes, awareness is sufficient; sometimes, action is desirable but that requires awareness as well.
